title: Investigation of the effects of the cannabinoids THC and CBD on central vestibular function
summary:
This observational study investigates whether medical cannabis affects balance function. THC and CBD are commonly used to treat chronic pain but may cause dizziness, unsteady gait, and an increased risk of falls. These effects may impair everyday mobility and safety, particularly in older people.

In patients who start physician-prescribed medical cannabis treatment for chronic pain, balance, visual stability during head movements, gait, and postural stability will therefore be assessed before and after treatment initiation. In addition, blood concentrations of THC, CBD, and their main metabolites will be measured. Three treatment groups receiving medications with different THC/CBD contents will be compared. The aim is to identify and better understand possible effects of treatment on the balance system at an early stage.

interventions.name: Central vestibular parameters, as well as gait and postural stability, will be assessed at several time points during cannabis treatment: before administration, shortly after administration, and several weeks after initiation of treatment. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Clinical indication for cannabinoid therapy  
- Age between 18 and 90 years  
- Written informed consent obtained after patient information and counselling  
- Ability and willingness to cooperate with study procedures
Exclusion criteria:
- Individuals unable to provide informed consent  
- Pregnancy  
- Pre-existing central or peripheral vestibular impairment (vestibular loss or other underlying neurological conditions that may affect the vestibulo-ocular reflex [VOR])  
- Current opioid therapy
